subject: Cognitive Science
title: Concepts in AI
description: A short lesson to help you apply Concepts in AI.

hook.text: A neural network labels a photo "husky" because of snow in the background, not the dog's features.

buildup.text: Machines learn categories from statistical patterns in data, without understanding what things are.

discovery.text: Human concepts carry causal knowledge—machines just have correlations with no explanatory depth.

twist.text: Yet large language models now pass tests of analogy and abstraction that once seemed human-only.

climax.text: Whether AI has true concepts or just convincing imitations remains cognitive science's hottest debate.

punchline.text: Machines classify, but do they understand?

quiz.question: How do AI categories differ from human categories?
options: AI relies on correlations; humans use causal understanding

details.summary: AI systems learn categories from data using deep learning, but their concepts differ fundamentally from human ones. Neural networks exploit statistical patterns, sometimes relying on shortcuts humans would never use.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding how AI categorizes reveals both the power of statistical learning and its limits. Human concepts are more flexible, robust, and theory-driven than current AI achieves.
takeaways: AI learns categories from statistical patterns in data
Machine concepts lack causal understanding and theory
Adversarial examples expose fundamental gaps in AI categories

faq.question: Why do adversarial examples fool AI but not humans?
faq.answer: Tiny pixel changes invisible to humans can flip AI classifications from panda to gibbon. This happens because AI relies on statistical texture patterns rather than structural understanding. Humans recognize objects through shape, function, and theory, making them robust to such perturbations.

faq.question: Will AI ever form concepts like humans do?
faq.answer: Current deep learning lacks causal reasoning, embodied experience, and theory formation that ground human concepts. Some researchers are building these into AI systems. Whether machines can achieve truly human-like conceptual understanding remains an open and actively debated question.
